brief: Fog-teal drench, a 98% readout settling at the treeline, pale-mint light, the morning stated in three facts.
rationale:
The phrase is a weather readout, three raw facts stated flat: fog, fifty degrees, calm. It is signal-event, not composed, because the morning handed me a 98% humidity figure and a 2.2 mph wind and the honest move is to format them, not embroider them. That phrase is a figure day: the humidity leads at poster scale and the line is its caption, which is why the composition is a figure object in the lower third of a near-empty field, the fog holding the upper two-thirds and the readout settling at the treeline.

Because the line is calm and cold, the field is one committed teal drench at 165°, inside the color mandate, with a single pale-mint light where the figure sits. No second accent, no neutral void: fog is one color at volume. The chassis is Source Serif 4, the one literary quiet face in the catalog that has not shipped, and the loudness guidance reserves the quietest heroes for lines that do not want shouting. A fog stillness does not shout; a warm text serif at a light weight reads as a contemplative morning, not a scoreboard.

The layout is the gold-standard split: the morning on the left, the selected work on the right, both drenched teal at two values so the division is weight, not a seam. Shell is footer-only, nav deferred to a flooded colophon band that reverses the signals out of the field, with the stacked-lg mark top-left of the fog so the brand is in the first fold at both widths. Motion is a wipe, the hero clearing in left to right like fog lifting, over a mesh ground that drifts slowly, the only moving thing a cold morning would actually do.

hero.rationale:
This morning in Aldie is one unambiguous fact: 98% humidity, fog to the ground, 49.9°F, wind at 2.2 mph. That is a weather readout stated plainly, the three facts formatted into one terse line, condition, temperature, and the calm of near-zero wind. It beats the Morrison quote because the quote is beautiful but it is not Doug's register; a weather readout in short fragments with real numbers is exactly how he clocks a morning. The Pistons loss and the market tick are lesser signals and go to the colophon.
Owner's voice: Doug says what a morning is in three facts and no adjectives, a score is a score and so is the fog.

3. Render feasibility: Yes — the figure at 120px (chassis 5xl max) and the phrase at 3xl fit a half-column at 1440 with room to spare.
4. Canvas floor feasible: Yes — two filled teal halves at measured density clear 70%; the empty upper-left fog is an intentional caesura inside a filled field.
5. Phone: Yes — split becomes a sequence; the 98% figure at 5xl (64px) and the phrase caption land inside the first fold, no word cut.

adBrief.compositionRationale: I moved `columns` off the suggested `three` to `two-equal` because the fog readout wants the gold-standard thesis/evidence split: the morning on the left, the work index on the right, both drenched teal so the division is value, not void. verdicts.feedback: [check 2] The largest first-fold text measures 300px at 1440; the declared hero_scale clamp(80px, 9vw, 120px) resolves to 120px there (250%, over the 75-125% band). Set the hero element's font-size to exactly clamp(80px, 9vw, 120px).

1. (Judgment 3) Type Treatment declares `alignment: centred`. At 1440 the hero stack is flush left in the left column: the HUMIDITY · ALDIE label, the 98% figure, the rule, the phrase and the deck. Only the mark is centred, so the page contradicts itself. Centre the figure, its label, the phrase and the deck on the fog field's axis, and carry the same alignment into fold 1 at 360.
2. (Judgment 6) SHELL declares `ground_material: mesh`, but the fog field at 1440 and in fold 1 at 360 is one flat teal with no visible bloom. Paint the radial mesh into the hero field so it reads as diffused fog, without dropping the reading text below its contrast floor.
3. (Judgment 5) Fold 3 reads "Doug March — product designer and frontend engineer." The record's role is "Product Designer & Developer." Use the recorded role.

2. Legibility: in the left fog field at 1440 and in fold 1 at 360, the mesh bloom washes out parts of the h1 and the deck. "FIFTY", "DEGREES," and "CALM." fade toward the ground, and "Wind 2 mph" and "Sunrise 7:41" nearly disappear into the dark patch. The bloom seems to sit over the type or to be part of its ink, not behind it. Raise the phrase and the deck above the mesh layer and give them a solid fill in primary or secondary text. The fog can drift behind the readout, but it must not eat the readout.

1. (Judgment 6) SHELL declares `ground_material: mesh`, but the fog field and the index field render as flat solid teal at both widths. There is no radial bloom anywhere. Paint soft mesh blooms into the hero field so the declared radial fog ground is actually visible.

2. (Judgment 3) The composition declares `hero_zone: lower-third` with the upper two-thirds left as empty mist. At 1440, the 98% figure sits near the vertical middle of the left column, and the mark, name and outlined ALDIE crowd the top of the field. Drop the figure, phrase and deck into the bottom third of the left column, and let the space above the mark breathe as open field.

3. (Judgment 2) The micro labels read as roughly 9–10px pale tint on teal at 1440: "SELECTED WORK", "FEATURED", "HUMIDITY · ALDIE", and the row metadata "SAAS · 2025" / "AI · 2026". That is below the brief's own 13px `xs` floor and too faint to read. Raise these labels to at least 13px and set them in the secondary text colour (`#b2d2c9`).
